questions.q: How long did Solomon take to build his own palace?
questions.a: Solomon took 13 years to build his own palace.

questions.q: What forest did Solomon use to build his palace?
questions.a: Solomon built his palace from the Forest of Lebanon.

questions.q: How big was the Porch of Pillars at Solomon’s palace?
questions.a: The colonnade at Solomon’s palace was 50 cubits long and 30 cubits wide.

questions.q: With what was floor of Solomon’s Porch of Justice covered?
questions.a: The floor of Solomon’s Porch of Justice was covered with cedar wood.

questions.q: What did Solomon build for his wife, Pharaoh’s daughter?
questions.a: Solomon built a house like his own for Pharaoh’s daughter, his wife.

questions.q: How big were the foundation stones of the buildings?
questions.a: The foundation stones used for the buildings were eight and ten cubits in length.

questions.q: How many rows of cut stones did the great courtyard surrounding the palace have?
questions.a: The great courtyard surrounding the palace had three rows of cut stones.

questions.q: Who came to work with bronze for king Solomon?
questions.a: Hiram came from Tyre to work with bronze for King Solomon.

questions.q: How many pillars of bronze did Hiram make?
questions.a: Hiram made two pillars of bronze.

questions.q: What was included at the very top of the pillars?
questions.a: There were two hundred pomegranates in rows at the top of the pillars.

questions.q: How many oxen did the sea stand on?
questions.a: The sea stood on twelve oxen, with three facing north, south, east and west.

questions.q: What was the height of the ten bronze stands that Hiram made?
questions.a: The height of each of the ten stands was three cubits.

questions.q: What were the wheels underneath the panels made of?
questions.a: The wheels underneath the panels were made of cast from bronze.

questions.q: How much water could each of Hiram’s basins hold?
questions.a: Hiram’s basins held 40 baths of water per basin.

questions.q: Did Hiram finish the work in the temple of Yahweh?
questions.a: Yes, Hiram finished all of the work that he did for King Solomon in the temple of Yahweh.

questions.q: How many pomegranates did Hiram make for the decorative latticework?
questions.a: Hiram made 400 pomegranates for the decorative latticework.

questions.q: What did Solomon use to make all of the furnishings in the temple of Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon used gold to make all of the furnishings in the temple of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Solomon put in the storerooms of the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon put into the storerooms all of the silver, gold and furnishings that David his father had dedicated.

commentary.text: Verses 1–12 All Solomon's buildings, though beautiful, were intended for use. Solomon began with the temple; he built for God first, and then his other buildings. The surest foundations of lasting prosperity are laid in early piety. He was thirteen years building his house, yet he built the temple in little more than seven years; not that he was more exact, but less eager in building his own house, than in building God's. We ought to prefer God's honour before our own ease and satisfaction.

The two brazen pillars in the porch of the temple, some think, were to teach those that came to worship, to depend upon God only, for strength and establishment in all their religious exercises. “Jachin,” God will fix this roving mind. It is good that the heart be established with grace. “Boaz,” In him is our strength, who works in us both to will and to do. Spiritual strength and stability are found at the door of God's temple, where we must wait for the gifts of grace, in use of the means of grace. Spiritual priests and spiritual sacrifices must be washed in the laver of Christ's blood, and of regeneration. We must wash often, for we daily contract pollution. There are full means provided for our cleansing; so that if we have our lot for ever among the unclean it will be our own fault. Let us bless God for the fountain opened by the sacrifice of Christ for sin and for uncleanness.

Christ is now the Temple and the Builder; the Altar and the Sacrifice; the Light of our souls, and the Bread of life; able to supply all the wants of all that have applied or shall apply to him. Outward images cannot represent, words cannot express, the heart cannot conceive, his preciousness or his love. Let us come to him, and wash away our sins in his blood; let us seek for the purifying grace of his Spirit; let us maintain communion with the Father through his intercession, and yield up ourselves and all we have to his service. Being strengthened by him, we shall be accepted, useful, and happy.
